item.title: Solved: How to Manage Variable Scope in PHP Applications
item.description:
“Solved: How to Manage Variable Scope in PHP Applications”

How is Variable Scope Defined in PHP?

PHP primarily employs function scope as its main scope separator. Variables defined within a function are strictly local to that function and cannot be accessed from outside. Conversely, variables declared outside of any function reside in the global scope. They are accessible anywhere else in the global context but remain inaccessible inside any function without explicit measures.

item.title: How does the global keyword work in Python
item.description:
“How does the global keyword work in Python”

Modifying Global Variables Inside Functions

When you need to modify a global variable within a function’s local scope:

counter = 0

def increment():
    global counter  # Declare we're using the global variable
    counter += 1

increment()
print(counter)  # Output: 1

Without the global declaration, Python creates a new local variable instead:

counter = 0

def wont_increment():
    counter = 5  # Creates a new local variable

wont_increment()
print(counter)  # Output: 0 (global unchanged)
